title: Nettle and Her Wobbly Shadow
markdown:
Nettle the goat was having a most peculiar day. She loved her big green meadow, dotted with bright happy daisies and bursting with yummy sweet clover. Munch, munch, munch. But something was wiggly. And wobbly. And just plain weird. It was her shadow.

“Hee hee,” she giggled, watching it stretch out long and skinny behind her like a giant sleepy worm. It tickled her hooves when she wiggled her nose. Then — zoom! — she scampered to a patch of buttercups, feeling very speedy. And guess what? Her shadow shrank. It became short and stout, like a tiny little Nettle tucked right under her feet.

“Whoa,” she bleated. Her fluffy white tail gave a confused twitch. She trotted away from the buttercups, and her shadow stretched out long again.

Wiggle, wobble, shadow.

“Why are you so tricky?” she grumbled, giving it a playful nudge with her nose. It just wobbled back, as if to say, I’m right here. “This is a puzzle,” she declared, her little goat brain whirring.

Just then a little light flickered, like a tiny star dancing near the ground. It was Fable the firefly, doing his speedy zig-zaggy dance in the air. Blink, blink, blink. He loved to zip and zoom and light up the world. He saw Nettle looking all bewildered, fuzzy ears flopped a little. He landed gently on a tall blade of grass. His glow made the grass sparkle.

“What’s wrong, Nettle?” he buzzed, a cheerful little hum.

“My shadow!” Nettle stamped a little hoof on the soft ground. “It keeps changing size! First it’s as long as a wobbly worm doing a stretch, and then it’s as short as a ladybug taking a nap! I don’t understand why it plays these silly tricks. Is it a mischievous shadow goblin?”

Fable giggled, tinkly. “Not tricks. Light! The big bright light.” He zipped up toward the golden sun. “The sun is a giant spotlight.” When Fable shone high, Nettle’s shadow sat small and neat under her hooves.

“Whoa,” she whispered. Hide-and-seek.

Then Fable zoomed down to the tall flowers at the meadow’s edge and shone from there, lower, nearer the grass. “Now look!”

The shadow ran out long and wavy, a furry brown river that almost reached the oak.

“It’s huge. A super-duper long Nettle!”

Wiggle, wobble, shadow.

Nettle trotted toward Fable’s glow: shorter, shorter. She ran back to the middle: longer, longer, a happy yawn of dark. “When the light is far and low, my shadow is long. When the light is close and high, my shadow is small. The light paints me on the ground, and I can change the picture by moving!”

Fable looped. “That’s how shadows work. You block the sunshine. How big they look depends on where the light comes from.”

Nettle nibbled clover, tail delighted. “Not tricky. Sciencey. Because of the light!” She looked at the warm sun, then at the short Nettle-shape she could stretch with a few steps. “I wonder what else the light can do. Rainbows? Taller flowers?”

Fable blinked his happiest blink, ready. Wiggle, wobble, shadow — and what other secrets were hiding in plain sight?
